name: Microdisney
label: Rough Trade
lede: Two Cork kids met at a New Year's Eve party, stuck record labels on other bands' sleeves at Rough Trade, and made pop songs so sweet that it took a minute to notice how hard Cathal Coughlan's words were biting.

eras.title: Punk at the Downtown Kampus
eras.text: Late-1970s Cork had blues bands, pub rock and heavy industry going under. Elvera Butler's Arcadia Ballroom gave the city's punks a stage, and Cathal Coughlan and Sean O'Hagan started a band there that began loud and turned, within two years, toward the Beach Boys and Scott Walker.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Irish Times · Wikipedia: Cathal Coughlan
years.h: Coughlan and O'Hagan meet at a New Year's Eve party in Cork
years.p: Coughlan, from the village of Glounthaune outside the city, and O'Hagan, a guitarist, start writing together almost at once.

years.cap: Coughlan and O'Hagan on stage in Cork
years.src: Wikipedia: Kaught at the Kampus
years.h: Microdisney plays the Arc, and a borrowed mobile studio rolls tape
years.p: Promoter Elvera Butler records four Cork bands live at the Arcadia Ballroom for Kaught at the Kampus. Microdisney's contribution is "National Anthem".
years.xp:
Butler had been entertainments officer at University College Cork, and her dry venue became known as the Downtown Kampus. She borrowed the mobile studio from Belfast. The EP came out in 1981 on her Reekus label, with Nun Attax (later Five Go Down to the Sea?) on side one.

In August 2020 Cork put the sleeve up as a mural on Grand Parade for the gig's 40th anniversary.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 2 · Wikipedia: Microdisney
years.h: "Hello Rascals": the first single, and the band shrinks to two
years.p: The early line-up had two lead singers and a hardcore edge. By 1982 Microdisney is Coughlan and O'Hagan, listening to Brian Wilson, Big Star, Erik Satie and Suicide.
years.xp: Perfect Sound Forever lists the new reference points: the Beach Boys, Scott Walker, Gram Parsons, Big Star, Satie, John Cage and Suicide. The early singles came out through Kabuki Records, with a second, "Pink Skinned Man", following in 1983.

eras.title: Two navvies at Rough Trade
eras.text: In London the pair had no money and plenty of songs. They worked for their own label by the piece, picked up a rhythm section, and by the end of 1985 had the record that topped the indie chart and still turns up on lists of the best Irish albums ever made.

years.src: Irish Times · Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 2
years.h: The ferry from Ringaskiddy, then sticker duty at Rough Trade
years.p: Coughlan and O'Hagan land in Kensal Rise and sign to [[Rough Trade|4f4b0013-1704-4936-a769-e6e8a6e08ff8]]. To make rent they do piecework at the label, putting stickers on records.
years.xp:
Rough Trade's Richard Boon remembered them as "two unemployed Irish navvies in London" doing piecework. Coughlan recalled re-sleeving [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]] records when the label hit trouble over a Terence Stamp cover photo.

The deal came after another fell through: Mike Alway was interested for Blanco y Negro but judged the album "too rocky", and [[Geoff Travis|70437714-3183-4916-947f-e5ba2154d16a]] signed them to Rough Trade instead. Cherry Red's publishing arm paid a £100 advance, which O'Hagan negotiated from a phone box in Kensal Rise.

years.src: Wikipedia: Microdisney · Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 2
years.h: John Peel takes them on: six sessions by 1986
years.p: Between 1983 and 1986 Microdisney record six Peel Sessions for BBC Radio 1. Some fans still prefer those takes to the studio versions.

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 2 · Paul McDermott
yt: Live at the Rock Garden, London, June 1984
years.h: Richard Boon finds a bassist: Jon Fell, plus Tom Fenner on drums
years.p: The duo becomes a band. [[Jon Fell|aefab8b4-8920-4158-82c8-92edce5c693b]] would later follow O'Hagan into [[The High Llamas|df3131d7-9cbc-4ad5-945a-09e979f003f4]].

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 2 · Wikipedia: Microdisney
years.h: Everybody Is Fantastic, Rough Trade's ROUGH 75
years.p: Recorded with producer Steve Parker in a converted church near Ladbroke Grove. It reaches No. 6 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp: Its release ran into a media strike, and reviews were mixed: some critics thought the drums sounded thin and preferred the Peel Session versions. "Dolly", produced by John Porter off the back of his Smiths work, was the single.

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 2 · Perfect Sound Forever
years.h: We Hate You South African Bastards! takes aim at apartheid
years.p: A mini-album of early singles under a title aimed at the apartheid state. The NME printed it as We Hate You White South African Bastards! with no explanation.

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 2 · Perfect Sound Forever
years.h: Gdańsk, Wrocław, Łódź: a tour of Communist Poland
years.p: The band plays behind the Iron Curtain and crosses East and West Germany by road. Part 2 of the band's radio history calls the tour a financial catastrophe.
years.xp: Perfect Sound Forever says the austerity they saw sharpened the politics in Coughlan's writing. Coughlan also talked about a deep paranoia attached to being Irish in London while the armed struggle was going on.

years.h: Microdisney on The Old Grey Whistle Test
years.p: The BBC show catches the band in 1985, the year of The Clock Comes Down the Stairs, playing "Loftholdingswood" among others.

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 2 · Irish Times · Wikipedia: Microdisney
years.h: The Clock Comes Down the Stairs goes to No. 1 on the indie chart
years.p: That's producer Jamie Lane's description of the record. Cut in his home studio in Balham, it tops the UK indie chart on November 23 and stays on it for 20 weeks.
years.xp:
Lane and engineer Bill Gill made the album fast and close to the band's own ideas. The sleeve photo, railway lines at Clapham Junction, is by Felicia Cohen.

O'Hagan's father had died the year before while the band was out supporting Violent Femmes in Birmingham, and the band's radio history hears that loss in the record. In 2018 it won the first IMRO/National Concert Hall Trailblazer Award.

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 2 · Perfect Sound Forever
years.h: James Compton takes over keyboards, freeing Coughlan to front
years.p: Nick Montgomery had come in on keys so Coughlan could work the stage, then left. James Compton fills the spot.

eras.title: Virgin, a barge, and a call from Coughlan
eras.text: The indie No. 1 brought the majors, and Virgin won. Microdisney got radio play, a chart single and a Bowie bill, and less than two years after signing they were finished.

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 3
years.h: Virgin wins the bidding for Microdisney
years.p: A&R man Ronnie Gurr signs them. What drew him was the pull between the two writers: "oil and water", he called it.

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 2 · Irish Times
years.h: Supporting the Go-Betweens at the Town & Country Club
years.p: Two bands of exiles living hand to mouth in London, which is how [[Robert Forster|c790898c-8e86-470c-88de-3d2c7560db10]] of [[The Go-Betweens|2fb4db11-8349-47ab-b1a6-f04f011699ff]] remembered it.
years.xp: "Neither band had any fall back," Forster said in the radio documentary. "You just had to get money for the next meal."

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 3
years.h: Virgin opens a Dublin Megastore, and the band plays from a barge on the Liffey
years.p: For the launch of the Virgin Megastore in Dublin, Microdisney play on a barge moored on the river.

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 3 · Perfect Sound Forever
years.h: Lenny Kaye produces Crooked Mile for Virgin
years.p: Recorded at Jam Studios on Tollington Park with Patti Smith's guitarist at the desk. Perfect Sound Forever calls it overproduced, a rock record that wasn't the band's style.
years.xp: Kaye was Virgin's suggestion. "We liked him and thought he was nice," O'Hagan said later.

years.cap: Microdisney at St Katharine Docks, London, March 26, 1987
years.src: Wikipedia: Microdisney · Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 3 · Perfect Sound Forever
years.h: "Town to Town" climbs to No. 55, and Radio 1 plays it
years.p: Their only UK top 75 hit. It reaches No. 30 in Ireland and is still on Irish radio.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever
years.h: "Singer's Hampstead Home" takes a swipe at Boy George
years.p: The first single from the next album. Perfect Sound Forever calls it a blatant mocking of [[Boy George|2787bddf-6439-4c73-8162-5f4a1e5fa030]].

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 3 · Wikipedia: Microdisney
years.h: Jamie Lane comes back for 39 Minutes
years.p: The Clock producer returns for the second Virgin album. "Gale Force Wind" reaches No. 98 in March.

q: Things were just building up in a very negative manner.
years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 3 · Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia: Microdisney
years.h: A Bowie benefit at the Dominion, then Coughlan picks up the phone
years.p: At the Intruders at the Palace benefit, on a bill with [[David Bowie|5441c29d-3602-4898-b1a1-b77fa23b8e50]], Microdisney sound like a band in a nervous breakdown. Days later Coughlan calls O'Hagan to say it can't go on.
years.xp:
"Things were just building up in a very negative manner," Coughlan said in the radio documentary. Perfect Sound Forever says Virgin ended the contract before a planned album with producer Don Was could be made.

Neither of them stopped. Coughlan formed [[The Fatima Mansions|d29658ea-c7d1-45a1-b272-9628a06c28e9]] the same year; O'Hagan went on to [[The High Llamas|df3131d7-9cbc-4ad5-945a-09e979f003f4]] and to work with [[Stereolab|f1df0431-9250-4ec8-95d8-f19ce7cf7fb6]].

eras.title: Two bands out of one
eras.text: The split gave Irish music two careers that went in opposite directions: Coughlan's Fatima Mansions loud, furious and profane, O'Hagan's High Llamas lush and Beach Boys-bright. Microdisney itself waited for a radio producer to tell its story.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cathal Coughlan
years.h: Coughlan names a band after a Dublin housing estate
years.p: [[The Fatima Mansions|d29658ea-c7d1-45a1-b272-9628a06c28e9]], named for the public housing complex in Rialto, release Against Nature, with songs like "Blues for Ceausescu".

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 3 · Paul McDermott
years.h: O'Hagan starts the High Llamas
years.p: O'Hagan's new band chases the Brian Wilson side of Microdisney. Jon Fell plays in it too.

years.src: Paul McDermott · Wikipedia: Microdisney
years.h: Paul McDermott's radio documentary gets the old band talking
years.p: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, made with University College Cork, airs on Newstalk. O'Hagan doubts the reunion would have happened without it.

eras.title: The clock comes back down
eras.text: Thirty years on, Microdisney played The Clock Comes Down the Stairs to people who had waited the whole time, then stopped again on purpose. Coughlan kept making records almost to the end.

years.cap: O'Hagan and Coughlan back on stage, c. 2018
years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia: Microdisney
years.h: Thirty years later, the National Concert Hall and the Barbican
years.p: Microdisney reunite to play The Clock Comes Down the Stairs in Dublin and London. The album takes the first IMRO/NCH Trailblazer Award.

years.src: Iron Fist in Velvet Glove, Part 3 · Wikipedia: Microdisney
yt: The Night, live in Dublin, Feb 18 2019
years.h: Last shows in Dublin and Cork, and that's it
years.p: Two final nights, February 18 and 19. Coughlan told the Irish Times the band had run its course.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cathal Coughlan
years.h: Cathal Coughlan dies in London at 61
years.p: He died at the Royal Marsden Hospital after three years of treatment for cancer, according to Wikipedia. His second album with Jacknife Lee as Telefís came out after his death.

years.src: Wikipedia: Microdisney
years.h: BBC Four tells the story of The Clock Comes Down the Stairs
years.p: A TV documentary on the band's formation, career and reunion.
